title: multi-gpu-parallelism-interconnect-characterization-wip
content:
Summary:

This is a working investigation into multi-GPU communication bottlenecks we observe in the serving runtime when using tensor- and pipeline-parallel execution modes. Focus areas: NCCL performance and rendezvous patterns, NVLink vs PCIe behavior, inter-node interconnect (Ethernet/InfiniBand), and how pipeline staging amplifies communication overheads. Goal is to identify practical mitigations we can implement in the runtime (kernel placement, fused comm, pipeline staging policy, fallback routing).

Background / Motivation:
- Several production workloads have intermittent latency spikes and throughput drops when model sequence length or batch size changes.
- Hypothesis: communication patterns across tensor/pipeline parallel boundaries (AllReduce/AllGather/ReduceScatter) are hitting interconnect limits or causing head-of-line stalls in the runtime scheduling.
- We need concrete profiling to guide fixes: is the issue link bandwidth, NCCL algorithm selection, serialization on CPU, or scheduling-induced idle time?

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Hardware tested: DGX-A100 (8x A100, NVSwitch), single-node 4x A100 with NVLink, 8x A100 across two nodes (Mellanox HDR InfiniBand), 4x A40 PCIe-only instance.
- Models: 13B decoder-only (fp16/qat8), 70B transformer (activation checkpoints enabled), micro-batch sizes [1,2,4], sequence lengths [128,512,1024].
- Parallel modes: pure tensor parallel (TP) 1..8, pipeline parallel (PP) stage counts 1..4, and hybrid TPxPP configurations used in production.
- Workloads: steady-state generation and bursty request pattern (Poisson arrivals) to reproduce queuing effects.

Tools and instrumentation:
- Nsight Systems (nsys) traces for cross-GPU timelines (GPU kernels, memcpy, NCCL ops).
- Nsight Compute for kernel-level hotspots where applicable.
- NCCL logging (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO/WARNING) and nccl-tests (all_reduce, all_gather, reduce_scatter) microbenchmarks.
- perf / bpftrace for CPU-side serialization points.
- iperf/rdma-bandwidth/ib_write_bw for raw link diagnostics in multi-node runs.
- Instrumented runtime traces (request start/queue/dequeue/kv-load/forward/comm/finish) with per-token timing.

Representative findings (initial):
1) NVLink (single-node) case:
   - Microbenchmarks show NVLink aggregate BW ~75% of theoretical on our 4x A100 testbed (consistent with expected headroom). Observed ~180-220 GB/s for pairwise communications depending on topology.
   - Nsight timelines reveal frequent small NCCL AllGather calls (~1-2MB each) coming from attention KV exchange in TP. The overhead of many small collectives causes latency blowups more than raw BW limits.
   - NCCL chooses ring algorithm for several sizes; switch to tree algorithms reduces latency for medium messages in some configurations.

2) NVSwitch/DGX (8x) case:
   - Aggregate throughput is good for large payloads, but we observe tail latency spikes when pipeline stages complete simultaneously causing synchronized AllReduce windows. This synchronization amplifies contention and causes queuing in the runtime.

3) PCIe-only hosts (A40 or vGPUs):
   - Lower sustained BW and higher latency; AllReduce costs dominate earlier (smaller sequence lengths). For production targets we should avoid TP across PCIe-only nodes for latency-sensitive routes.

4) Multi-node (InfiniBand HDR) case:
   - Raw link BW is high; however, inter-node latency and software stack (verbs, HCA driver) add 5-15us per collective step compared to NVLink.
   - Topology-aware placement (keep PP stages local and minimize cross-node TP partitions) improved throughput 10-25% in our runs.

5) Pipeline parallelism interaction:
   - PP introduces bursty communication at micro-batch boundaries: when a stage flushes, it issues large inter-stage transfers. If multiple micro-batches align, we see spikes.
   - Staggering micro-batches (offset by a small number of tokens / time) reduces peak concurrent comms and smooths bandwidth utilization.

6) CPU serialization and NCCL launch overhead:
   - In several runs, CPU-side serialization (locking and queuing in the runtime message path) is responsible for 10-30% of observed NCCL call overhead. Profiling shows significant time between scheduling the NCCL kernel and actual GPU work in high-concurrency cases.

Quantitative examples (typical):
- 13B model, TP=4, seq=512, batch=2 on 4x A100 NVLink: mean token-latency 55ms, 95p 110ms. Switching to tree algorithm for NCCL AllReduce reduced 95p to 88ms.
- Same model across 2 nodes (4 GPUs each) with PP=2 hybrid: mean token-latency 72ms, 95p 190ms; moving PP boundaries to be node-local reduced 95p by ~25%.

Root-cause hypotheses we intend to validate:
- Small-message collectives created by KV exchange dominate latency; NCCL algorithm selection is not always optimal for our message size distribution.
- Pipeline-stage synchronization creates momentary spikes of concurrent collectives leading to queueing and CPU-side contention.
- Cross-node splits of tensor partitions amplify latency due to extra hop and verbs overhead.

Short-term mitigations to evaluate in runtime (prioritized):
1) Collective fusion: batch small NCCL ops into fewer larger collectives where correctness allows (e.g., pack small KV blobs).
2) Dynamic NCCL algorithm override: based on message size and topology, prefer tree-/recursive doubling over ring for latency-sensitive sizes.
3) Micro-batch staggering / skewing: introduce a small configurable offset between micro-batches to avoid synchronized flushes.
4) Topology-aware partitioning: prefer partitions that keep PP boundaries on the same node when latency SLOs are tight.
5) Offload NCCL launch sequencing to a dedicated communication thread pool to reduce CPU-side serialization.

Longer-term directions:
- Investigate hardware offload options (GPUDirect Async, RDMA-aware kernels) to reduce CPU path.
- Explore model-level KV cache layouts to reduce shuffle size (compress/pool KV slices).
- Integrate an adaptive planner in the orchestration layer that picks TP/PP layouts given expected request mix and SLOs.

Immediate next steps / experiments to run (next 2 weeks):
- Implement microbenchmark harness that reproduces attention KV exchange sizes for our 13B and 70B models; run nccl-tests across those exact message size distributions. (owner: Ben)
- Prototype collective fusion in a local runtime branch and measure latency/peak BW impact. (owner: Asha)
- Add per-NCCL-op timestamps in runtime traces and re-run production trace that produced the original spike with debug sampling. (owner: Lina)
- Run placement-aware experiments for multi-node hybrid TP/PP to quantify benefit of node-local PP (owner: Tom).

Open questions / risks:
- Correctness impact of packing/fusing collectives for model state (must ensure order and atomicy semantics).
- Interaction with quantization/packing: fused buffers may interact poorly with int8/qat paths.
- Operational complexity: topology-aware scheduling requires integration with cluster topology service; cost of implementing vs benefit needs to be justified.

Appendix: quick checklist of artifacts to capture with each run:
- nsys trace (.qdrep) + compressed timeline png (nsys-ui).
- NCCL logs for every rank of the job.
- nccl-tests output with sizes aligned to our KV microbenchmark.
- Runtime per-request trace with per-phase timing (queue, kv-load, forward, comm, finish).
- Kernel summaries from Nsight Compute for hotspots.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; please add experimental suggestions, topologies we should test, or known vendor guidance (NVIDIA best-practices) to the Confluence page linked above.
- If you have baseline numbers for other infra (e.g., DGX-H100), add them as comments or in the experiments sheet linked in Confluence.

Acknowledgements: Ben, Lina, Tom for initial traces and helping with nccl-tests.

End of doc.
